4 Forwarded by coordinator

Yes, you can test it on your Windows PC in about 10
minutes:

1. Get the files. Download & sema-v0.1.zip , or use
Code > Download ZIP on GitHub. Unzip it
somewhere like C:\Sema.
. Install Python 3.12 from python.org. In the installer,
tick “Add python.exe to PATH”.
. Double-click setup .bat . It installs everything and
starts Sema. A round purple icon appears in the
system tray, near the clock.
. Try It. Select some text In Word, Outlook, Chrome or
anywhere else, then press Alt+Shift+S. Press
Alt+Shift+O and drag a box around anything on
screen to read it with OCR. Alt+Shift+P pauses and
resumes.
. Browser extension (optional). Open
chrome: //extensions or edge://extensions and
turn on Developer mode. Click Load unpacked and
choose the extension folder. Then right-click the
Sema tray icon, choose Copy browser pairing code,
and paste the code into the extension’s Settings.

For a quick listen without installing anything, the
& Sema Preview still works. This will be the first time
Sema runs on real Windows, so if anything doesn’t work,
tell me what you saw, or send the log at
%APPDATA%\Sema\sema. log , and I'll fix it.
